processes.description: A coordinator circulates a monthly notice of counterparty name changes and mergers, first as an initial notice and then as the final list for the month. The reference data team announces when it will apply the changes in the system, and risk staff forward the list onward and remind their groups to use it.
steps: Collect the month's counterparty name changes, mergers and inactivations.
Send the initial merger and name change notice for the month.
Issue the final list for the month once changes are confirmed.
Announce when the changes will be applied in the reference system and apply them.
Forward the list to desk staff and remind them to use the updated names.

automation.approach: Keep the counterparty change list in one shared register that feeds the reference system, and generate the initial and final monthly notices from it, with a scheduled update window stated in each notice.
automation.rationale: The work is a recurring list moving from initial to final and then into the system; a standard list layout reduces retyping and makes it clear which version desks should use.

work_estimate.rationale: Compiling and checking the month's name changes and mergers, then entering them in the reference system at the announced time. The quotes show the list and the scheduled update but not its size, so the range is wide.

processes.description: Risk and logistics staff spot deals sitting in the wrong book, or deals that must be killed or terminated, and send lists asking the book owner to flip them, often right away or by the next day. In the bankruptcy period, termination lists and contract lists arrive repeatedly, deals are moved into the bankruptcy books, stragglers follow, some deals are moved back to live books, and the risk side cross-references the final list against its calculations.
steps: Identify deals that sit in the wrong book or must be killed or terminated.
Compile a list or spreadsheet of deal numbers with source and target books.
Send the list to the book owner or risk group asking for the move.
Flip the deals in the trading system and confirm they have been moved.
Handle follow-up lists of stragglers and any reversals back to live books.
Reconcile the final list of moved deals against risk calculations and transfer numbers.

stalls.summary: Risk waits on a final list of terminated deals to cross-reference while more straggler lists keep arriving.
Confusion about a specific deal requires a phone call, and a question about who changes the counterparty on a sale shows unclear handling.
A proposed index book waits on a reply, and a reporting system fails to print.

contradictions.summary: Ownership of terminations and estate risk is named differently: one sender says she and Darron will handle terminations from now on, while another says Greg Couch will lead the estate risk effort.
Deals are sent to be moved into the bankruptcy books, then the same requester asks for transactions to be moved from the bankruptcy book back to the live side.

automation.approach: Use one standard deal-move request sheet (deal number, source book, target book, trader, reason) and a daily report that matches termination lists against current book assignments, flagging deals not yet moved and any reversals.
automation.rationale: Requests arrive as ad hoc lists in many formats and are repeatedly followed by stragglers; a single layout and an automated match against the master termination list cut rework and make reconciliation straightforward.

work_estimate.rationale: Building the deal list, looking up each deal's current book, flipping the deals in the system and checking the result against termination lists or transfer numbers. Many rounds cover a few deals; bankruptcy rounds cover longer lists and reconciliation, hence the high end.

processes.description: As staff move to the new employer, HR and infrastructure teams send notices about orientation sessions split by alphabetical order, benefits presentations, new hire paperwork due by 3:00 PM on a stated day, missing application details, outstanding pre-employment drug tests, access card pickup and email file migration with compliance forms. Staff complete the paperwork, tests and migration steps; a planned system migration was postponed.
steps: HR announces orientation sessions and benefits presentations.
HR sets a deadline for new hire paperwork and flags incomplete applications.
HR reminds individuals of outstanding pre-employment drug tests.
Staff collect access cards and export their email per migration instructions.
Teams batch file migration compliance forms and send them in.
Infrastructure migrates users to the new environment or announces a delay.

stalls.summary: The email export route loses attachments, and the planned migration to the new environment was postponed.
Paperwork comes back incomplete and pre-employment tests remain outstanding, prompting individual reminders; one notice reached the wrong person.

automation.approach: Track each transferring employee against one onboarding checklist (orientation, paperwork, application, drug test, access card, email migration, compliance form) and send reminders automatically from the outstanding items.
automation.rationale: The notices repeat the same handful of requirements to many people, and the reminders show items being chased one by one; a shared checklist makes status visible and drives the reminders.

work_estimate.rationale: Checking records for missing paperwork or tests, completing forms, attending to migration steps and compiling compliance forms. Each round centres on one requirement, so the hands-on part is modest.
